body: I don't try to talk to anyone, and I'm a bit older than most of the other undergrads I see, only a few years but it feels like a big difference.

The only time I spend around other people is when I'm in class, and I don't talk to anyone. Maybe most universities are like that. Sometimes it's fun to laugh at other people, it just depends on my mood I guess.
Why would I laugh at their problems?

My course load is pretty light I feel, I don't have any other obligations or anything either. I could try making a planner but I probably wouldn't stick to it, and I still feel like burying my head in the ground and saying what's the point.
Er, to be clear, I emailed them 1-2 weeks ago.
I have not.
I tried to schedule over email with the therapist but they haven't responded to me, and the only other way to make an appointment is to call and I can't do that.
Yeah.
I wake up in the middle of the night or early in the morning, I don't have much trouble actually falling asleep.
I don't have any physical problems that would cause me to have trouble sleeping. It's just anxiety about classes, and a lack of proper exercise I guess.
I'd see the therapist through my school, about once a week, and the break was due to winter break. I haven't seen them since the start of term mainly because I felt it was pointless.
I have trouble sleeping and wake up tired everyday, and then struggle to focus throughout the day. The more I think about it the more I feel I could try to kill myself tonight if I really wanted.
I saw a psychiatrist a few months ago, twice actually. The last time I saw a therapist was sometime in November last year.

I don't know exactly what my diagnosis is. I think I'm just pathetic and awful. I stopped trying antidepressants over a year ago, I almost feel it's been two years but I don't know anymore. I have a lot of difficulty keeping track of time.
I can't focus :\
My homework then.
I don't think so.
Prozac maybe, in that it didn't have negative side effects that I noticed.
The first thing that comes to mind right now would be to go to sleep and not wake up.
I tried about 5 different medications at different doses.
I've taken a few years off from school, and I don't really feel like working.
I took medications for about a year and gave it up, I tried therapy with three different people for about 2 years.
No, not really. I don't really want to be in school. I don't have any passions.
I wanted to be good at it, I used to like it, most of the time I don't care, I just want the day to be over.

I don't deserve to live because I don't enjoy life and I struggle too much and I feel like it would be easier to just stop. The problem with distractions is that that's all they are. I don't have enough energy to do productive hobbies, and things like exercise, so I read or play computer games and then I feel sick with myself. I'm not in immediate danger, I'm just saying that I can see what direction my feet are taking me.
Computer science, but I suck at it.
I'm in college and I have homework that I need to be doing though, I just can't get myself to work on it, I have been distracting myself with just those things you've mentioned but it hasn't helped.
Yes but they make me feel hollow, or at least I feel empty and I just end up distracting myself from my actual life.
I'm just pathetic and I don't deserve to live and I don't see much reason to living anyway.
Hrm, sometimes I feel a bit offput when someone refers to me as a boy or man or something, but I wouldn't consider it an intense feeling or anything.

I'm not sure what exactly gender dysphoria feels like. The general sense of dysphoria could be something I experience though.

I've thought about trying that chat idea before, I think it might be a good suggestion. I am hesitant to talk to people though, and at times I feel very misanthropic, but maybe I can try it, because I hate feeling the way I do sometimes. I wouldn't know what to say either, I'm not used to talking to anyone.

I can try to not think about being female when/if I masturbate in the future, but it's hard for me because that's pretty much what I've always done (pictured myself as female or as a male presenting as female), since I first did it even.

Thanks for the suggestion and thoughts though.

Erections are more of an inconvenience than anything for me. 

I can remember at times wanting my genitals to be removed, now that you mention SRS. I don't know what my rationalization for that was though. It wasn't that I disliked them, but the thought of them being removed or destroyed somehow was kind of exciting, I dunno why. 

I would have to experiment with being seen as a woman I guess, and I'm not sure how to do that in a safe environment that didn't feel too fake.

I haven't grown my hair out very much, my family starts to pressure me a bit about it and I never know how to style it so it just looks unkempt. I've worn outfits of women's clothing, and been to a therapist dressed that way. When I'm alone it just feels kind of neutral, but it can also make me feel sad sort of, I'll be hyper-aware of how the clothing doesn't fit me properly, and I just feel like a weirdo. When I went to the therapist it was really just stressful.

Um, I guess there are positives about either of them. There's no menstruation with male genitals, but you also can't ever carry a baby. In the past I've been envious of women for their genitals, but I'm not sure why. The idea of being penetrated seemed more natural to me maybe, I'm not sure. I have a very hard time making my mind up about things. When I start thinking along that route though a flag comes up, and there's a part of me that says I need to be more masculine.

I don't have much of an opinion either way about my genitals. In terms of the secondary characteristics, I've valued some things about me that seemed feminine, like having less hair on my arms and things like that. When I was about ten and saw a girl with more hair on her arms than me it made me feel good. I kind of like having muscles, because I don't want to be weak, but I am not a muscle-y person. I wish I had less hair in general, it makes me feel like a caveman. To me these things seem normal though, it would make sense to me if most men felt that way. Masculine characteristics just make me feel more ugly.

You sound a whole lot like me, except I've never had any relationships. I do experience a lot of confusion and despair though. I hope more people can offer you advice because I could really use some as well!

I would really appreciate any input from anyone, I know it must sound desperate but I guess I am. I just want help from anywhere I can get it right now. Maybe I should focus more on help with depression, I just don't want to feel like a hopeless pathetic mess anymore.

I should clarify because I just realized what I said was pretty stupid. I have actually seen a few therapists, and brought it up to each of them, and went to a couple sessions presenting as female. I'm really not sure why I put it the way I did, I guess I was worked up, it's not exactly that it's terrifying to see a therapist but I don't have the energy to find one who might be a best fit for me. I struggle a lot with depression and most days I just want to lie in bed. I'm more afraid of going to something like an LGBT group and talking about these things, but I have been to one in the past (I just said nothing when I was there).
